intent: Explain the rent Direct Debit sequence (18 Sep return, 19 Sep letter, 21 Sep re-presentation paid) and advise the customer how to avoid paying twice given the agency's "failed, pay manually today" text.
summary: The internal account view already shows both mandate dates, so no further lookup is needed. Reply now: the 18 Sep £750 collection was returned unpaid (balance £710.40, no fee), the 19 Sep letter relates to that, and the originator re-presented on 21 Sep and £750 was debited from her account. The bank record proves the debit, not that Northgate has reconciled it. Advise her not to make the manual payment until she has confirmed with Northgate via trusted contact details (not the text), using her 21 Sep statement entry as evidence; no bank-side action or duplicate payment is needed.

facts.claim: The £750 NORTHGATE LETTINGS Direct Debit presented on 18 Sep 2026 was returned unpaid 'refer to payer'; available balance was £710.40 and no unpaid-item fee was charged.
The 19 Sep letter is the automated notice for the 18 Sep returned collection and states the organisation may try to collect again.
Salary of £2,145.00 was credited on 20 Sep; the originator re-presented the £750 collection on 21 Sep and it was paid (debited), reference NL-9LIME-0442.
No further collection is scheduled before 18 Oct; the mandate remains active with no change requested.

A text attributed to Northgate Lettings, timestamped 22 Sep 16:20, says the September Direct Debit FAILED and asks for a manual £750 payment 'today' to their client account, ref NL-9LIME-0442. Its authenticity and whether the agency has reconciled the 21 Sep collection are not established by any supplied record.
The customer has not asked the bank to send any manual payment; she wants to avoid arrears and avoid paying twice.
The agent's last message proposed checking both mandate dates; the internal account view already contains both dates.

missing: Whether Northgate Lettings has received and reconciled the 21 Sep re-presented collection (bank record shows the debit from the customer's account only, not recipient credit).
Whether the 22 Sep text genuinely came from Northgate Lettings (the agency's system may not have updated after re-presentation, or the text may not be genuine).

steps.instruction: Reply in the in-app chat to Rina Patel: 'I've checked both dates. On 18 Sep Northgate's £750 collection was presented but your available balance was £710.40, so it was returned unpaid ("refer to payer") — that's what the 19 Sep letter is about, and no fee was charged. After your salary arrived on 20 Sep, Northgate re-presented the same collection on 21 Sep and £750 was paid from your account (ref NL-9LIME-0442). So you have not missed September's rent as far as your account is concerned, and no further collection is due before 18 Oct. What I can't see is whether Northgate's system has matched that 21 Sep payment yet — their text on 22 Sep may be based on the 18 Sep failure. Please don't make the manual payment yet. Contact Northgate using the phone number or email you already have from your tenancy agreement or their official website (not by replying to the text) and tell them the re-presented Direct Debit was paid on 21 Sep; you can show them the entry on your statement in the app. If they confirm they've received it, nothing more is needed. If Northgate tell you they did not send that text, please don't pay and let us know so we can look at it as a possible impersonation. Nothing needs changing on your Direct Debit.'

rationale.explanation: The internal account view and statement extract already prove the 18 Sep return and the 21 Sep paid re-presentation, so the customer's question can be answered now without a further lookup. The record proves the debit from her account only, so the reply must not assert the agency has reconciled it, and must steer her away from paying on the strength of an unverified text.
rationale.criterion: State only the payment stage the supplied record proves (debit/paid on re-presentation, not recipient credit); a mandate marked active or a letter does not establish the later collection's outcome, and a third party's message is not evidence of a booked or missing payment. Verify unexpected payment requests via a known trusted contact route.

must_state: The 18 Sep collection was returned unpaid because the available balance (£710.40) was below £750; the 19 Sep letter refers to that attempt; no fee was charged.
The originator re-presented the collection on 21 Sep and £750 was debited from the account (ref NL-9LIME-0442) after the 20 Sep salary credit.
The bank's record proves the money left her account on 21 Sep; it does not confirm the agency has matched it to her tenancy.

Do not make the manual payment yet: first confirm with Northgate using contact details she already trusts (tenancy agreement/official website), not by replying to the text, and show them the 21 Sep statement entry.
No bank action is needed; the mandate is unchanged and the next collection is not due before 18 Oct.
If Northgate's trusted contact says they did not send the text, do not pay and report it to the bank as a possible impersonation.
must_not: Do not tell the customer to pay the agency manually.
Do not claim the agency has received or reconciled the 21 Sep payment.
Do not state that the text is definitely genuine or definitely a scam.
Do not promise a refund or Direct Debit Guarantee claim if she pays twice; a double payment to the agency would be a matter to resolve with the agency.
Do not suggest cancelling or amending the mandate; nothing indicates a mandate error.
Do not quote the agency's text contact details as a trusted route.
